item.title: Domain Adaptive Graph Neural Networks for Neutrino Experiments
item.description: arXiv:2611.10057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weakly interacting particles such as neutrinos require highly efficient and precise detection methods to enable searches for new physics. Deep learning, and particularly Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), has shown promise for reconstruction tasks in liquid argon time projection chamber (LArTPC) neutrino experiments. However, differences between simulations and experimental data introduce domain shifts that can degrade model performance and potentially mimic or obscure new-physics signals. Here, we demonstrate that robust learning across datasets can still be achieved by using domain adaptation during training. We introduce, to our knowledge for the first time, domain-adaptation-enabled GNNs for robust LArTPC reconstruction tasks. We use MicroBooNE open dataset as our labeled source domain, and introduce four perturbed datasets as our unlabeled target domains-- including a fixed scale variation, moderate and severe gaussian noise, and a signal variation as a function of the position in the detector. The inclusion of adversarial-based domain adaptation during training improves performance for all four target domains, without a substantial drop in performance in the source domain. Precision in the target domain was improved up to 0.19 and recall up to 0.37, depending on the variation and the network task. These results demonstrate a potential of domain adaptation to bridge the gap between simulations and experiments, and build more trustworthy models for current and future LArTPC neutrino experiments.
item.dc:creator: Hemalata Nayak, Giuseppe Cerati, Aleksandra \'Ciprijanovi\'c, Tammy Walton

item.title: Distinguishing thyroid nodule malignancy using digital palpation
item.description: arXiv:2611.12563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate pre-operative diagnosis of thyroid nodules remains a major clinical challenge. Current diagnostic techniques rely on fine-needle aspiration and demonstrate high rates of inconclusive results, often leading to avoidable thyroidectomies with lifelong implications. Here, we introduce a mechanics-based diagnostic method that leverages Digital Palpation to determine malignancy and identify tissue subtypes in human thyroid nodules. From a cohort of patients undergoing thyroidectomies, we evaluated ex vivo thyroid specimens and processed the resulting mechanical data from 36 tests in 10 thyroid nodules. Principal Component Analysis reveals that these experimental results are distributed within a three-dimensional space of interpretable scalar features reflecting tissue grittiness, strength, and toughness, which map closely to descriptions of malignant and benign nodules given by clinicians. Our results further demonstrate that malignant nodules exhibit distinct mechanical signatures compared to their benign counterparts. This revealed a statistically significant difference (p = 9 x 10^-4) and separability (95% lower-bound Hedges' g = 1.08) between benign and malignant nodules along a direction in principal component space representing effective stiffness. Preliminary clustering patterns were also observed among malignant subtypes, including follicular, oncocytic, and papillary thyroid carcinomas. Together, these results highlight the potential of Digital Palpation as a novel mechanics-based method for tissue characterization and motivate its further development toward diagnostic applications.
item.dc:creator: Brendan M. Unikewicz, Joseph E. Bonavia, Ekaterina L. Koelliker, Abigail Klein, Katie C. Spaeth, Hannah M. Varner, S. Kiana Naghibzadeh, Yoav Horev, Sareh Parangi, Tal Cohen

item.title: Beyond node strengths: the topological content of weighted bipartite networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.10085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weighted bipartite networks encode the topology and intensity of interactions between two disjoint sets of nodes. However, it is unclear whether the observed pattern of connections is already explained by node interaction volumes or contains additional structural information. Here we introduce a hierarchy of maximum-entropy models for continuous weighted bipartite networks that preserves node strengths alone, strengths and global density, or strengths and the complete degree sequence. Across economic, technological, ecological, social and lexical systems, we find that strength constraints alone are generally insufficient to reproduce empirical structures. Yet the missing topological information is often low-dimensional: a single constraint controlling network density frequently provides the most parsimonious description, whereas networks with stronger residual degree heterogeneity require node-specific constraints. Beyond downstream inference, we also show how the choice of topological resolution changes which interactions and projected relationships are identified as statistically significant. Our results indicate that topology is essential, but often compressible, in the statistical modeling of weighted bipartite networks, and provide a scalable computational framework for fitting, sampling, model selection and validation within a common workflow.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Cirulli, Lorenzo Buffa, Giulio Cimini, Dario Mazzilli, Aurelio Patelli, Fabio Saracco

item.title: Test beam results for machine-learning-based reconstruction of resistive silicon sensors
item.description: arXiv:2611.10194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The advent of Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (LGADs) and AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) as candidate technologies for four-dimensional tracking has moved part of the reconstruction burden onto the analog waveforms of the sensor, in which the charge shared between electrodes encodes the impact position well below the electrode pitch. Recovering that position is a continuous, non-linear inverse problem. Transient Current Technique measurements characterize this problem at fixed injected charge and high signal-to-noise, whereas a minimum-ionizing beam adds Landau fluctuations in the deposited charge under detector operating conditions. We report test beam results for full-waveform reconstruction of an AC-LGAD of 500 $\mu$m pitch read out on a $2\times2$ pad matrix, exposed to the 120 GeV pion beam of the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) and read out alongside a six-plane MIMOSA-26 telescope. The telescope is aligned, and its per-plane resolutions are calibrated in situ, giving a track pointing resolution of about 2.5 $\mu$m per axis at the device, so that the measured residual is the sensor response rather than a convolution with the reference. We then compare two analytic estimators, the parameter-free charge-imbalance formula and a fitted linear matrix inversion, with the topology-agnostic transformer developed for resistive silicon sensors. Over the full active pad, the transformer reaches a median total position with up to factor 3 improvement. Within the charge-sharing core, the three methods converge to the floor of this sensor at the achieved signal-to-noise.

item.title: FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge: Dataset and Cosmological Inference Competition
item.description: arXiv:2611.10228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weak gravitational lensing is a powerful cosmological probe that enables direct mapping of the matter distribution and precise constraints on the fundamental parameters governing structure formation in the universe. In recent years, machine learning has shown strong potential for extracting cosmological information from weak-lensing data beyond traditional summary statistics. However, progress has been limited by the lack of standardized benchmarks that capture the complexity of the dataset, simulator imperfections, and various systematic biases encountered in realistic analyses. To address this gap, we present the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing Machine Learning Uncertainty Challenge, one of the NeurIPS 2025 competitions, as a benchmark dataset and evaluation study. Our dataset reflects realistic weak-lensing observations, incorporating multiple systematic biases, and thereby providing a controlled testbed for robust cosmological inference under uncertainties. We summarize the main methodological advances developed by the winners of our challenge, including data augmentation with conditional optimal transport, an AI-agent-driven approach for parameter inference, ensemble learning, Vision Transformer-based architectures, and physics-informed feature integration. By unifying the benchmark dataset and the winning solutions, this work provides a community resource for developing and evaluating machine learning methods for weak lensing cosmology and, more broadly, for scientific inference under systematic uncertainties.

item.title: Causal discovery from Bayesian symbolic regression
item.description: arXiv:2611.12458v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Causal discovery from observational data is central to scientific reasoning, yet established constraint-based and score-based methods often recover only a Markov equivalence class and provide no signal in bivariate or strongly autocorrelated regimes typical in some areas of science. Here, we recast causal discovery as a Bayesian symbolic regression problem. Given a set of candidate parents for each target variable, the Bayesian symbolic regression samples closed-form expressions from a posterior over symbolic models. The fraction of sampled expressions in which each candidate variable appears defines a posterior inclusion probability that we use as the causal score. This replaces pointwise model selection by an ensemble of plausible mechanisms. We evaluate the method on coupled nonlinear bivariate dynamics, on the CauseMe benchmark suite spanning linear, chaotic, nonlinear, higher-dimensional and high-noise settings, and on a four-variable biogeoscience structural causal model under Gaussian, heavy-tailed and mixed-noise regimes. Our approach is competitive with, and often outperforms, specialized causal discovery algorithms. Additionally, the method returns closed-form mechanisms leading to explicit causality and interpretability.
item.dc:creator: Roger Guimer\`a, Kai-Hendrik Cohrs, Sergio Pedreira, Marta Sales-Pardo, Gustau Camps-Valls

item.title: A regularization-independent Information Criterion for correlated data
item.description: arXiv:2611.12877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We generalize the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) to allow model and data subset selection when regularized fits are performed on correlated data. While the standard generalization to regularized fits is inherently dependent on the type of regularization applied to the data covariance matrix, our definition, the RIAIC, is, on average, regularization-independent. The regularization-independence is achieved by defining the new Information Criterion as an estimator of the model-dependent contribution to the correlated Kullback--Leibler divergence. The Bayesian extension is derived as well. We test the new criterion on lattice QCD data by performing regularized fits and show that it reproduces the selection properties of the standard correlated AIC, with fluctuations which are compatible with the expected statistical uncertainties. These results enable the application of subset and model selection techniques to cases where regularizations are applied to the covariance matrix of the fitted dataset.
item.dc:creator: Davide Laudicina

item.title: Shaking the causal tree: On the faithfulness and minimality assumptions beyond pairwise interactions
item.description: arXiv:2203.10665v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Higher-order mechanisms can make genuine causes invisible to causal discovery, but whether this reflects fine tuning or a structural limitation remains unclear. We prove, for a binary causal family, that the failure of faithfulness is not a measure-zero pathology: it persists for every nonzero coupling vector, even though every active edge remains causally minimal. Experiments with established causal-discovery methods show how this separation propagates into algorithm-dependent failures. A Partial Information Decomposition then identifies the lattice supports probed by faithfulness and minimality, placing the two premises at opposite ends of a single conditioning hierarchy. This exposes a two-sided obstruction: synergy can erase faithfulness, while redundancy can make the positive margin protecting minimality arbitrarily weak. Exact causal premises and practical discoverability can therefore point in different directions
item.dc:creator: Tiago Martinelli, Diogo O. Soares-Pinto, Francisco A. Rodrigues

item.title: Meteosat Third Generation imagery improves CNN-based SSI retrieval
item.description: arXiv:2607.28093v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate Surface Solar Irradiance (SSI) estimation is increasingly important for photovoltaic energy monitoring and forecasting. The recently introduced Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) satellite constellation provides imaging data with higher spatial resolution compared to the Meteosat Second Generation (MSG) satellite constellation, but its benefits for machine-learning-based SSI retrieval are not well established. We compare multi-resolution convolutional neural network models for 10-minute SSI retrieval over Northern Europe (Estonia) using either MSG/SEVIRI or MTG/FCI satellite imagery. We evaluate model performance against ground-based pyranometer measurements from eight Estonian meteorological stations using site-based cross-validation with a temporally independent test year and multiple training seeds. Model performance is also compared with the SARAH-3 physics-based satellite SSI product. The FCI-only model significantly outperformed the SEVIRI-only model under overcast and cloudy conditions, reducing RMSE by 5.1 W/m^2 and 6.5 W/m^2, respectively. However, under partly cloudy or clear skies, there was no statistically significant difference in RMSE between the FCI-only and the SEVIRI-only models. In all-sky conditions, the RMSE of the FCI-only model was 5.1 W/m^2 lower on average, but this difference was not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. Compared with physics-based SARAH-3, the FCI-only model yielded skill scores of 28% under overcast conditions, 19% under cloudy conditions, and 17% overall. Furthermore, both models underperformed SARAH-3 in clear-sky conditions. These results show that higher-resolution MTG/FCI imagery improves CNN-based SSI retrieval when clouds dominate irradiance variability, but also indicate that higher resolution alone is insufficient to address clear-sky limitations in machine-learning-based SSI retrieval.
item.dc:creator: Gordei Prib\~otkin, Piia Post, Velle Toll

item.title: From populations to absolute binding affinities in molecular simulations: exact volumetric terms and practical estimators
item.description: arXiv:2608.04834v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Biomolecular simulations of binding commonly confine the unbound ligand with volumetric restraints to accelerate convergence. However, a general account of how such restraints enter the volumetric term of the standard binding free energy, and of how this term should be evaluated from histogram data, is currently lacking. We take as our starting point the established relation, in the dilute limit, between the binding constant $K$ and the relative populations of the bound and unbound states, which we re-derive from the canonical partition function of molecular solutes in explicit solvent. Building on this relation, we show that a restraint that leaves the bound state unaffected and confines a homogeneous unbound region modifies the volumetric term in a single way, by replacing the system volume with the volume of the region over which the unbound population is evaluated. This yields closed-form estimators for restrained simulations, computable from histograms of any suitably defined reaction coordinate, with the volumetric term kept explicit. Previous expressions based on the potential of mean force are recovered as a special case. The analysis also exposes two distinct errors in current practice: single-bin estimators, which reduce the bound state to one histogram bin and are not valid estimators of $K$, and working formulas that omit the bin width entering the volumetric term, which make the result depend on the unit of length. We apply the estimators to a Lennard-Jones dimer, the cucurbit[7]uril/1-adamantanol host--guest complex, and the galactonate--DgoT ligand--protein complex.
item.dc:creator: Davide Mandelli, Emiliano Ippoliti, Charles Plate
